deferred_human_review_runtime: Library issue for @941design/nostr-events maintainers: the simple-pool transport de-duplicates by event id BEFORE signature verification, so a relay sending a forged event that reuses a genuine event id first gets the forgery rejected AND the genuine event dropped as a duplicate (message-suppression by a hostile relay). Found by app/tests/unit/marmot/client/transport.forgery.harness.test.ts. Not fixable in-app without a custom verifier (AC-TRANS-1 forbids one).

S3 accepted residual: if the account is torn down (sign-out/signer change) while a withdrawn message dispatch is still running past its 10 s bound, its late retract is dropped and the withdrawn message stays in the chat store. Requires a fork-withdraw + >10 s handler + teardown in the same window.

S5 decider (recompute-on-retract): after a fork rewind, edits/deletes/reactions/poll results are rebuilt from retained group history — a withdrawn delete or edit makes earlier content visible again, admin-gated deletes are re-judged against the CURRENT admin list, and the original text of an edited/deleted message stays on the device (in the history store and the slot base snapshot) until the group is left.

S5 accepted residual: votes are keyed by poll id, so if a poll open is withdrawn while ANOTHER member open for the same poll id remains (requires deliberate id reuse), earlier votes count toward the surviving poll. Live dispatch behaves the same.

S7: the library media codec drops http/loopback/private-host Blossom locators, so group images now require an https Blossom server. Default taken: keep the library rule; the e2e Blossom mock (and local dev) must be served over https (S24, via NEXT_PUBLIC_BLOSSOM_BASE_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_BLOSSOM_TRUSTED_HOSTS). Local `make dev` image sending against an http Blossom will fail loudly.

AC-SIGN-3 amended (S7 review): NIP-46 requested permissions now also include sign_event:24242 (Blossom upload auth for group images) and 25050–25055 (call signaling; previously missing). Existing bunker sessions recorded with the old set will be discarded once and must reconnect (AC-SIGN-4).

S8 product call: inviting a pubkey that already holds a leaf in the group returns already-member (no second leaf), so adding a SECOND DEVICE of the same account via invite is refused, although the library permits same-account device adds (its ADR-003). Few has no multi-device flow today; confirm this is intended.

S9 decider: invitation caps now retain TRUSTED sponsors first (own account or ever-known peer incl. contacts) and expire STRANGER invitations after 14 days (AC-CAP-1/D14 amended). Confirm the 14-day figure; under a sustained stranger flood a legitimate stranger invitation can still be silently lost (recovery: add as contact and re-invite); confirm a sponsor can re-invite after a silent decline (not verified in the library).

S9 residual (privacy, needs your call): a SILENT decline (blocked or over-cap sponsor) sends no rumor or wrap, but the library then rotates the consumed key package, publicly superseding the kind-30443 event the sponsor used — the sponsor can observe that its Welcome was processed and rejected (a per-decline receipt oracle). Options: accept, or ask the library for a silent decline that defers/skips rotation.
